target_customer: Cannabis brands, co-packers and manufacturers producing pre-rolls, infused products and vape cartridges
problem: Pre-roll and infusion production is labor intensive and inconsistent, so cannabis manufacturers need automation for filling, infusing and coating.
business_model: Hardware sales of automation machines plus custom integration services

founders.name: Nohtal Partansky
founders.background_notes: The YC page founders section is blank. Search results from trade press (not opened) name him co-founder and CEO and say he came from NASA-JPL; the company site says its machines are built by ex-NASA engineers.

founders.name: Cassio Santos Jr
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in trade press search results, not on an opened company page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Precision dosing, handling of sticky cannabis material and custom hardware with a small team in 2018.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware know-how and installed machines with customers create some lock in, but other equipment makers could build similar machines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Paxiom later sold JuanaRoll pre-roll machines and was acquired by ATS in July 2024; no incumbent acquired Sorting Robotics.

market_need_then: Legal cannabis expansion in 2018 and 2019 created demand for production automation; the company says it sold 250+ machines deployed worldwide (own site, self-reported).

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and industrial: 'A new era of cannabis manufacturing', 'Seeing is believing'

branding.brand_signature: Playful product names such as Jiko and Stardust
branding.community_and_virality: Customer brands such as Beard Bros Pharms published an article on Stardust; limited wider community evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Name described the original sorting product and no longer fits; product names are memorable within the cannabis trade.

pivots.from: Sorting product line for other industries
pivots.why: A YC job listing says the original product line was sold in fall 2019 to focus on cannabis; Machine Design dates the pivot to 2020 (sources conflict).

outcome_analysis: Sorting Robotics pivoted into cannabis automation around 2019 or 2020 and launched Jiko in 2021, Omnifiller in 2022 and Stardust, claiming 250+ deployments. Funding is small and mostly debt and crowdfunding, which suggests a capital light hardware business that has stayed alive but not scaled like a typical venture company.
notes: Founder names and the pivot timing come from search result summaries, not opened pages, so confidence is low. Sacra and Caplight list a $500K crowdfunding round in April 2024 and Sacra a $2.6M earlier seed; both are single aggregator claims and unverified. Totals conflict (CB Insights 2.15M, Sacra 3.5M, Caplight 5.25M). Competitor search found only undated or post-2021 pages (Paxiom JuanaRoll), so the list is empty.
